decisions.reason: As a recently launched line close to the core architectural hardware business, it is likely to be retained because tooling, design and market-entry investments have just been made and there is no clear evidence yet to justify reversal.
This handle family fits the established offer and broad portfolio logic, so management would likely continue with it rather than admit an early retreat from a fresh multi-model launch.
Although a single design is somewhat easier to discontinue than a full family, it is still close to the firm's core range and would likely be given more time before being judged unsuccessful.
Because it is a new core-range handle design in a growing industry, management would likely keep it on the market and attribute any slow uptake to normal ramp-up rather than to a wrong decision.
This multi-model handle family supports the firm's system breadth and established business, making withdrawal within a year unlikely given the recent investment and low strategic risk.

As a flagship electronic access system publicly presented as part of the firm's direction, it has the strongest sunk investment, strategic centrality and reputational commitment, so management would be especially reluctant to drop it quickly.
